title: feat(data): host-configured default and maximum page size for list, report and analytics reads, and a per-query row budget, refused with a code naming the limit
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-zhuang"} -->
_Requested by **Sam** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01GsBogozeZG5sdpAARrN7HP?thread=cmsg_01GsBogozeZG5sdpAARrN7HP1GdLsoH7z9V8sNW6YoLEMF)_

Part of #29783

This PR is the whole of that card. It says `Part of` rather than a closing keyword because the card's claim names no `claude/issue-*` branch and this PR's head branch cannot take that shape, so `check:closing-target-claim` could never pass with a closing keyword. The seat closes the card when this lands.

## What changes

A deployment can now bound how many rows one data API read returns and walks, through three host variables. Each is a positive integer; all three unset is today's behaviour exactly.

| Variable | Meaning | Unset |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `OS_DATA_DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE` | the page a read gets when it names no `limit` | the maximum when one is set, else no default |
| `OS_DATA_MAX_PAGE_SIZE` | the largest `limit` a read may name | no maximum |
| `OS_DATA_QUERY_ROW_BUDGET` | the most rows one query may walk: `offset` plus the rows it returns | no budget |

**The documented rule for a request over a limit is refuse, never clamp.** A clamp answers a different page from the one asked for: a caller paging by its own `limit` would skip the rows in between, and an analytics answer has no `hasMore` to say a chart was cut. So:

- a `limit` over the maximum → `400 MAX_RECORDS_EXCEEDED`, the existing standard code for a caller-side limit (the request asked for more rows than a request may carry), naming the spelling the caller wrote (`$top` / `top` / `limit`) and the maximum;
- `offset + limit` over the budget → `400 QUERY_ROW_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, naming the budget. This is a new code because the budget bounds how deep a query walks, not how big a page is: a page well within the maximum is refused at a deep enough offset.

Both are refused before the driver is asked (a budget probe, below, runs first and refuses on its answer). Each refusal writes one `warn` line: `[data] read refused: code=… surface=list|analytics object=… rows=… limit=…`. The line carries the object and counts, never a row value.

**A read that names no limit:**

- **List reads** (`GET /data/:object`, `POST /data/:object/query`, grouped or flat, through `findData`) run with the default page size as their `limit`. The answer already says when more rows exist (`hasMore`, `total`), so this is an ordinary first page.
- **Analytics reads** (`AnalyticsService.query()` behind `/analytics/query`, and `queryDataset()`, the dataset door reports and dashboards read through) run with one row more than the default page. An answer with more rows than the default is refused with `MAX_RECORDS_EXCEEDED`, telling the caller to name a `limit` and page with `offset`. The analytics doors judge the caller's own window; the dataset executor's internal passes (totals, measure-scoped queries) are not judged separately.
- **A budget with no page size** probes one row more than the budget leaves after the `offset`. An answer over the budget is refused, and one that fits is served whole (the probe limit is taken back off, so `hasMore` / `total` read as an unpaged answer).

**Where it lives:**

- `@objectstack/types` `query-read-limits.ts` holds the rule: `resolveQueryReadLimits` (strict: a value that is not a positive integer, or a default above the maximum, throws naming the variable), `planQueryReadWindow`, `assertQueryReadRows`, and the abstract `QueryReadLimitError` (`limit`) with one subclass per code, `QueryPageSizeExceededError` (`MAX_RECORDS_EXCEEDED`) and `QueryRowBudgetExceededError` (`QUERY_ROW_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`), each declaring its own `code` and `status 400` so `check:error-status-conformance` pins the catalog's status. `MAX_RECORDS_EXCEEDED` gains its first producer, so it leaves `scripts/error-status-unpinned-baseline.json` (the shrink-only direction).
- `metadata-protocol` `findData` plans every list read after the shape gates and before the engine.
- `service-analytics` `query()` and `queryDataset()` plan the caller's window at the public doors.
- Both constructors resolve the limits once, so a misconfigured variable fails the boot instead of 500-ing every read.
- `QUERY_ROW_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` is registered in the error-code ledger under `@objectstack/types`, with a line on why it is not `MAX_RECORDS_EXCEEDED`; the references pages are regenerated; `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx` documents the three variables and the refusal rule; `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx` gains a `QUERY_ROW_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` entry, names the page-size cause under `MAX_RECORDS_EXCEEDED`, and counts 57 wire codes.

**What the budget does not count:** rows a database scans inside an aggregate or behind an unindexed filter. The data API cannot see those, so the budget counts the rows a query walks through its window. The expand sub-reads, the export route and internal engine reads (backfills, sweeps) are not data API list reads and are untouched.

## Why

The maintainer's 2026-11-03 04:26Z instruction on the cloud plan decision, verbatim: 「同意：在代码里补两个保护再谈放宽：查询扫描行预算和强制分页；每周看板加「每个 Team 组织的数据库大小与行读量」。第 3 个月闸门前有这两组数，再决定存储包价格和数据边界的数字。」

The hosted data plane runs this data API, and on `main` there was no general page-size cap in it or in the SQL / libSQL drivers (re-checked at `946a173f`: `driver-odata`'s `pageSize` is only for its own upstream, and MCP's `maxQueryLimit` only for its own tool). Cloud sets the numbers in its own card (cloud#3510) once a pin carries this.

## Verification

- `packages/types/src/query-read-limits.test.ts` (18): configuration (unset, all three, strict refusal of `0` / `-5` / `1.5` / `abc` / `10k` / `1e3`, default above maximum), no limits leave every read untouched, refusal shape (status, code, `limit`, message, the one log line with no row value), the default page, the analytics probe, the budget (including the default page counting against it, and the budget-only probe), and both codes resolving verbatim at 400 through `resolveThrownHttpError`.
- `packages/rest/src/data-query-read-limits.test.ts` (6, real `SqlDriver` over SQLite, both list doors): defaults unchanged with nothing set (every row, a 100,000 limit, a grouped read), the default page with `hasMore: true` / `total: 5`, a limit within the maximum, `MAX_RECORDS_EXCEEDED` on `$top`, `top`, `limit` and a grouped read with the driver never called, `QUERY_ROW_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` with the driver never called, and a budget-only read refused when it overruns and served whole (`hasMore: false`, `total: 5`) when it fits.
- `packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/query-read-limits.test.ts` (8): both analytics doors unchanged with nothing set (no `LIMIT`, 500 rows served), the probe reaching the query (`limit: 4`) and the SQL (`LIMIT 4`), an answer past the default refused with the log line, a caller's own limit run as asked, over-maximum and over-budget refused with nothing run, and the budget-only probe.
- `data-page-window-door.test.ts` (the existing window pins) still passes. Full local suites: `types` 860 tests, `metadata-protocol` 310 files, `service-analytics` 4,958 tests, `rest` 7,139 tests, all passing.
- `pnpm typecheck` for `types`, `metadata-protocol`, `service-analytics` and `rest` (with its test layer); eslint on every touched file; `node scripts/check-error-status-conformance.mjs` green; spec `error-code-ledger.test.ts` green; `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` named `content/docs/references/**` stale, regenerated with `gen:docs`; `check-doc-anchors` resolves the new catalog links; `check-error-status-conformance` (and its self-test) green.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --tier`: no path-derived tier mandate. Its Clause ② hint fires on `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`: the new code widens the published `ErrorCode` vocabulary, so a contract-tier review is owed before the queue.

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

What Clause-② widens: the published error-code vocabulary. `ErrorCode` (the union `ApiErrorSchema.code` parses against) gains one registered member, `QUERY_ROW_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`. A page size over the maximum answers the existing standard `MAX_RECORDS_EXCEEDED` (400), which gains its first producer. No metadata an author writes changes, and no existing code, status or response shape moves.

_Keep one value on each of the two lines above, each line starting with its key.
[Human Minimum](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#human-minimum)
item 5 says what they mean._

## Human Minimum

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic.
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes.
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request.
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed.
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English.
- [x] The *Before Submitting* list in CONTRIBUTING.md is done.
